record.one_liner: Twilio SendGrid: email API and SMTP service for transactional and marketing email
record.auth_notes: Bearer API key per the v3 API docs; Basic auth with username 'apikey' also uses the API key, so it counts as api_key. No OAuth flow documented in the pages fetched.
record.access_notes: critic: access self_serve_free -> self_serve_trial. Twilio retired the SendGrid Free plan (May 27, 2025); the vendor pricing page now lists only 'Free Trial $0/mo for 60 days' (100 emails/day per secondary sources) before paid Essentials at $19.95/mo. API keys are created in the console Settings.
record.api_notes: REST v3 at api.sendgrid.com covering mail send, marketing contacts, templates, stats, suppressions.
record.blocker_notes: critic: mcp official -> community. Twilio's hosted mcp.twilio.com/docs is a docs-only server and its Twilio MCP targets Twilio's API, not SendGrid v3; no vendor action server found. Community servers (Garoth/sendgrid-mcp) exist. Trial lets developers get working keys, so verdict stays ready.

evidence.quote: Twilio SendGrid supports API keys delivered via Bearer token or Basic authentication, depending on the Twilio SendGrid functionality you are using.
Authenticate to the Twilio SendGrid API by creating an API Key in the Settings section of the Twilio SendGrid console.
include an Authorization header with the value Bearer <YOUR_API_KEY_HERE> in your request
